subject: Branching egress & streaming SLOs — post-demo qualification
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Nasser <amira@finsecure.com>; John Doyle <john.doyle@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Branching egress & streaming SLOs — post-demo qualification

Thanks again for your time during the demo earlier today — appreciate the candid discussion about streaming behavior when customers attach larger payloads. Per our call, I wanted to capture the open items we discussed and the minimal data we need to qualify a Private (VPC) pilot for streaming inference: 

1) Target latency SLOs (P95/P99) for single-stream responses at differing payload sizes (small / 1-5KB; medium / 5-50KB; large / >50KB).
2) Expected sustained concurrency (number of concurrent sessions) and burst concurrency (short spikes).
3) Typical throughput per session (tokens/sec or bytes/sec) and any jitter expectations.
4) Network path details: whether traffic will egress over a VPN, direct cloud peering, or via a NAT gateway; expected egress IPs, and presence of any intermediate proxy/load balancer.
5) A network diagram (simple, annotated) and a recent run of iperf or equivalent between your app hosts and the target VPC where Redwood Private would be deployed.
6) Any regulatory constraints around egress or TLS termination.

Action items I will own: provide a concise SLO profile template and a suggested smoke test plan (we'll include stream-level microbenchmarks and an example attack plan for egress-path fallbacks).

If you can drop the network diagram and the iperf output into the Drive link below, we can turn this into a scoped acceptance test and schedule a 90-minute network validation window next week.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/finsecure/project-network-diagram

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachment: redwood_slo_template.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)
From: Amira Nasser <amira@finsecure.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Doyle <john.doyle@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kyle Park <kyle@netops.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Branching egress & streaming SLOs — post-demo qualification

Alex — thanks for the recap and for the template. John and I pulled together the initial artifacts and Kyle (netops) is copied for the iperf run. Quick answers inline below, and I attached the network diagram and a CSV with our rough expected concurrency/throughput: 

- Latency targets: P95 <= 250ms, P99 <= 500ms for small payloads; for medium payloads P95 <= 350ms, P99 <= 700ms; large payloads target P95 <= 800ms. These are our business targets; happy to adjust if Redwood needs different bands for accurate qualification.
- Sustained concurrency: 120 sessions; burst up to 450 for short 60s windows (marketing campaigns).
- Throughput/session: average 600 tokens/min (approx 10 tokens/sec), but streaming payloads can push to ~25 tokens/sec during synthesis bursts. We included a CSV (streaming_slo_matrix.csv).
- Network path: we plan to use an IPSEC VPN tunnel from our on-prem gateway to the Redwood VPC peering endpoint. Egress will be NATed at our edge; we will provide the NATed IPs. There is an inline proxy only for outgoing HTTP inspection (transparent for TCP).
- Regulatory: No TLS termination at the edge; all traffic must be TLS 1.2+ end-to-end.

Kyle, can you run an iperf3 test against the candidate VPC endpoint (we'll share a target IP) and drop results to the Drive link?

Attaching: finsecure_network_diagram.pdf, streaming_slo_matrix.csv

Thanks,
Amira
VP Product, FinSecure
amira@finsecure.com

--

Subject: Re: Branching egress & streaming SLOs — post-demo qualification

Thanks Amira — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions so we scope the pilot correctly: 

- For the burst concurrency (450 for ~60s), can you confirm the pattern — is it an even ramp across sessions or a handful of heavy sessions? This affects KV/cache warmup and tail-latency behavior.
- On the IPsec VPN: are you provisioning static routes or will this be BGP-managed? Static routes will change how we recommend fallback policies.
- Can you share a sample of the largest streaming payload (redacted) so we can run tokenization and perf profiling ahead of the test? A single JSON blob is fine.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kyle to run iperf3 to our test endpoint and upload results to the Drive link by Monday 9am PT.
2) FinSecure to drop the largest streaming payload sample and NAT IP list into Drive.
3) We (Alex + Vivek) will produce a scoped smoke test plan and a canary schedule (45-min validation) and post it into the HubSpot deal record.

If all that looks good we'll lock a 90-minute network validation on Tue 2027-04-06 or Wed 2027-04-07 — pick your preference and we'll send a calendar invite.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
